children: The Indonesian rupiah is likely to face renewed depreciation pressure versus the dollar in September and October, UOB Kay Hian analyst Suryaputra Wijaksana says in a note. This is due to worsening global conditions, particularly the escalation of the U.S.-Iran conflict and rising oil prices. A potential Federal Reserve rate increase could also strengthen the dollar and weaken the rupiah. This could prompt Bank Indonesia to raise its policy rate and intervene to defend the rupiah. The dollar is 0.1% higher at 17,525 rupiah, LSEG data show. (amanda.lee@wsj.com)
